summary.en: Repeat code a counted number of times with initialization, condition and update on one line.
summary.bn: গোনা সংখ্যকবার কোড চালাও — শুরু, শর্ত আর আপডেট এক লাইনে।

notes: Declaring the counter inside the for header needs C99 or later.
C11, C17 and C23 made no changes to the for loop.

videos.note: For loop explained in Bangla with solved examples

examples.title: Print numbers from 1 to 10
examples.explanationHtml: int i = 1 runs once. Before each repetition C checks i <= 10; after each repetition i++ adds 1. The body runs 10 times.

examples.title: Bounded sum of 1 through n
examples.explanationHtml: For n from 1 to 1000000, sum receives every integer through n. The long long accumulator holds their total safely. A successful read and an explicit upper bound are checked before the loop begins.

examples.title: Multiplication table of a number
examples.explanationHtml: The number is restricted to -1000 through 1000, so multiplying by each table row from 1 to 10 fits int on the stated host. Width conversions align the columns.

examples.title: Reverse an array with two loop variables
examples.explanationHtml: The header declares two variables, left and right, and updates both with the comma operator. Each repetition swaps one pair, so an array of 6 needs only 3 swaps.

examples.title: Read marks until 0 with for (;;)
examples.explanationHtml: Zero ends the session, so it is not a data mark. Invalid mark ranges are skipped. At most 100 valid marks are accepted; the bound keeps both the count and total safe.

examples.title: Mistake: a semicolon after the for header
examples.outputNote: Prints only "i = 6": the loop finishes first, then printf runs once.
examples.explanationHtml: The semicolon is an empty statement that becomes the whole loop body. The indented printf is not part of the loop, which is exactly what GCC warns about (-Wmisleading-indentation). Remove the semicolon and add braces.

practice.title: Even numbers up to n
practice.statementHtml: Read n from 0 to 1000. Print even numbers from 2 through n, each followed by a space, then a newline. For n below 2 print only the newline.
hints: Start the counter at 2 and add 2 each time instead of checking every number.

practice.title: Factorial of n
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0 to 20) and print n! = value. Remember that 0! = 1.
hints: Use unsigned long long: 20! does not fit in an int.

practice.title: Multiples of 3 or 5
practice.statementHtml: Read n from 0 to 10000. Count and sum positive integers below n divisible by 3 or 5. Print count = C, sum = S and a newline. Count a shared multiple once.
hints: A number like 15 is a multiple of both; it must be counted once — use ||.

practice.title: Prime numbers in a range
practice.statementHtml: Read a and b with 0 <= a <= b <= 10000. Print each prime in that closed range followed by a space, then a newline. If no prime exists, print No primes and a newline.
hints: A number n is prime if no d from 2 to the square root of n divides it.
Write the condition as d * d <= n to avoid sqrt and floating point.

quiz.prompt: In for (initialization; condition; update), which part runs only once?
quiz.explanation: The initialization runs once before the first check. The condition is checked before every repetition and the update runs after every repetition.

quiz.prompt: The loop below stops when i reaches 3. Which digits does it print?
quiz.explanation: i takes the values 0, 1 and 2. When i becomes 3 the condition i < 3 is false, so 3 is never printed.

quiz.prompt: After this loop ends, what value does i hold when it is printed?
quiz.explanation: The loop stops only when the condition fails. That happens when i is 5, and i keeps that value after the loop.

quiz.prompt: This loop counts down by 3. What does it print before the condition fails?
quiz.explanation: i goes 10, 7, 4, 1. The next value would be -2, but -2 > 0 is false, so the loop stops before printing it.

quiz.prompt: Two loop variables move towards each other. Which pairs are printed?
quiz.explanation: The pairs are (0,5), (1,4), (2,3). Next i is 3 and j is 2, so i < j is false and the loop ends.

options: It is a compile error because the parts are empty
It repeats forever until break or return is used inside it
quiz.explanation: An empty condition counts as true, so the loop has no built-in end. Use break or return to leave it.

quiz.prompt: How many times does the body of for (int i = 1; i <= 100; i += 10) run?
quiz.explanation: i takes the values 1, 11, 21, 31, 41, 51, 61, 71, 81 and 91: ten values. The next value, 101, fails the condition.

quiz.prompt: The for body is empty, and count++ follows the loop. How many increments reach count?
quiz.explanation: The empty body runs three times without changing count. The single count++ statement after the loop runs once.

quiz.prompt: Which C standard first allowed for (int i = 0; ...) with the declaration inside the header?
quiz.explanation: C99 added declarations inside the for header. In C89 the counter must be declared before the loop.

quiz.prompt: Which loop is usually the clearest choice when you know the exact number of repetitions in advance?
quiz.explanation: The for loop keeps the start, stop and step on one line, which makes counted loops easy to read. A while loop is better when the end depends on input or an event.

quiz.prompt: The inner loop depends on the outer counter. What pattern is printed?
quiz.explanation: The inner loop runs i times on row i: 1 star, then 2, then 3. Each row ends with a newline from the outer loop.

quiz.prompt: Why does for (unsigned int i = 5; i >= 0; i--) never stop?
options: Because i-- is applied before the check
Because an unsigned value is never negative, so i >= 0 is always true
Because the loop has no braces
quiz.explanation: When i is 0 and you subtract 1, an unsigned int wraps around to a very large value. i >= 0 is therefore always true. Use a signed int for countdowns that reach 0.

keyPoints.en: A for loop repeats code a counted number of times.
keyPoints.bn: for লুপ নির্দিষ্ট সংখ্যকবার কোড চালায়।

keyPoints.en: Initialization runs once; the condition is checked before every repetition; the update runs after every repetition.
keyPoints.bn: শুরুর অংশ একবার চলে; শর্ত প্রতিবার আগে যাচাই হয়; আপডেট প্রতিবার পরে চলে।

keyPoints.en: Any part of the header may be empty; for (;;) loops until break or return.
keyPoints.bn: হেডারের যেকোনো অংশ খালি রাখা যায়; for (;;) চলে যতক্ষণ না break বা return আসে।

keyPoints.en: Use the comma operator to set or update two variables in one header.
keyPoints.bn: কমা অপারেটর দিয়ে এক হেডারে দুটো ভেরিয়েবল সেট বা আপডেট করা যায়।

keyPoints.en: A semicolon right after the header makes an empty loop body.
keyPoints.bn: হেডারের ঠিক পরে সেমিকোলন দিলে লুপের বডি খালি হয়ে যায়।

keyPoints.en: Declaring the counter inside the header needs C99 or later.
keyPoints.bn: হেডারের ভেতরে কাউন্টার ঘোষণা করতে C99 বা পরের সংস্করণ লাগে।

examQuestions.question: Write the general form of a for loop in C and explain the job of each of its three parts.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
for (initialization; condition; update) { body }

  • Initialization runs once, before the loop starts, and usually sets the counter.
  • Condition is checked before every repetition; the body runs only while it is true (non-zero).
  • Update runs after every repetition and usually moves the counter forward or backward.

examQuestions.question: Find the output: for (int i = 2; i <= 10; i += 3) printf("%d ", i);
examQuestions.answerHtml: 2 5 8 — i takes 2, 5, 8; the next value 11 fails i <= 10.

examQuestions.question: Write a C program that reads n and prints the sum of the series 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + ... + 1/n correct to 4 decimal places.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
#include <stdio.h>

int main(void)
{
    int n;
    double sum = 0.0;

    if (scanf("%d", &n) != 1 || n < 1) {
        return 1;
    }
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
        sum += 1.0 / i; /* 1.0 makes the division floating-point */
    }
    printf("%.4f\n", sum);
    return 0;
}

Marking notes: writing 1 / i instead of 1.0 / i gives integer division and a wrong answer.

examQuestions.question: Compare the for, while and do-while loops. When would you choose each one?
examQuestions.answerHtml:
• for: entry-controlled; initialization, condition and update on one line; best when the number of repetitions is known.
  • while: entry-controlled; only a condition in the header; best when the loop depends on input or an event.
  • do-while: exit-controlled; the body runs at least once; best for menus and input validation.
